You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Lanternix on this image exposes /app/bin/lanternix. That mill is a native ELF Go program; the file begins with 7fELF. A script or interpreter at that path is not enough. Cast and readout usage plus JSON field rules live in /app/notes/ROUTE.txt and /app/notes/GRAMMAR.txt. Cast writes generated units under /app/packbay/units and /app/packbay/reg.go. Repair the Go pipeline modules named in /app/notes/ROUTE.txt. Source edits under /app are required. Hand-written readout JSON is not enough.

On this image lanternix cast exits 0. readout of /app/lamps/flash9c.lamp exits 2 and does not write /app/glowbank/readout.json. A correct mill decodes any recipe lamp whose card the mill carries; readout slots must be the lamp file values as strings using the names from that card.

A recipe card whose id the mill does not carry makes readout exit non-zero and must not replace a success readout.json. A lamp whose code is absent from /app/cardwell still reports void and exits non-zero. The verifier reruns readout only.

Analysis: The notes define the three source areas and behavior. The project is a single offline Go module with four cards and generated unit packages already present. The attempted hex inspection failed because xxd is unavailable, and the binary type command produced no output, likely because file is unavailable or the binary is problematic. We now need inspect all Go sources, Makefile, and text fixtures directly to understand the broken cast/readout pipeline.
Plan: Print source and fixture files with clear delimiters, inspect binary magic using od, permissions with ls, and run the current commands while recording exit statuses and any existing readout. This will expose both implementation defects and current failure behavior before editing.

steps.message:
Analysis: The binary is already a native ELF Go executable. The defects are clear in generated registration: reg.go only loads units A/B, Pull only accepts two hard-coded IDs, generated slot names retain whitespace, and Spin always regenerates registration with only A/B. Play also appears to boot before Pull, so newly offered specs may not reach oxbind, and cardsCovered incorrectly makes every card in cardwell a prerequisite—contradicting the requirement that an uncarried ghost card must only cause its own recipe to fail without replacing a prior successful JSON. The current cast command was still running when output ended, so we should poll before editing. We also need retrieve the complete parser code omitted by terminal truncation.
Plan: Wait for the current command to finish, then print play.go in smaller numbered chunks. After that, replace the pipeline logic so cast parses all valid cards, deterministically generates units and reg.go for every carried known card, and rebuilds atomically. Readout will load the compiled registry, decode only the requested lamp, write success atomically, write void for codes absent from cardwell, and leave an existing success file untouched for card IDs present on disk but not compiled into the mill.

arguments.keystrokes: nl -ba /app/milldesk/play.go | sed -n '1,180p'
nl -ba /app/milldesk/play.go | sed -n '181,360p'; printf '\n--- post-cast generated files ---\n'; cat /app/packbay/reg.go; for f in /app/packbay/units/*/pack.go; do echo ===$f; cat "$f"; done

steps.message:
Analysis: Cast fails because Spin regenerates an incomplete registry and the pipeline initialization is ordered incorrectly. Card slot parsing preserves spaces, only two hard-coded codes are loaded, and readout globally rejects any extra card rather than distinguishing an uncarried card from an absent code. We need make cast regenerate a complete deterministic registry from cards, make boot populate the store before snapshotting it, and implement the required failure/output preservation semantics.
Plan: Rewrite oxbind initialization, make packbay loading generic, simplify cast dispatch, and replace readout with card-aware logic and atomic JSON writes. Rewrite Spin to trim/validate cards, refresh all generated unit directories and reg.go, and compile/rename the ELF atomically. Then format, build the current mill, run cast to generate the final carried registry and rebuild itself, and test all supplied lamps plus ghost-card and absent-card preservation behavior.

arguments.keystrokes: /app/bin/lanternix cast; echo cast_rc=$?; od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/lanternix; cat /app/packbay/reg.go; for f in /app/packbay/units/*/pack.go; do echo ===$f; cat "$f"; done

rm -f /app/glowbank/readout.json; for l in warm beam flash9c held; do /app/bin/lanternix readout --lamp "/app/lamps/$l.lamp"; r=$?; echo "$l rc=$r"; cat /app/glowbank/readout.json; done
printf 'id: LAN_GHOST_77\nslots: x, y\n' > /app/cardwell/ghost.card
printf 'CODE LAN_GHOST_77\nx=one\ny=two\n' > /tmp/ghost.lamp
cp /app/glowbank/readout.json /tmp/before.json
/app/bin/lanternix readout --lamp /tmp/ghost.lamp; echo ghost_rc=$?; cmp -s /tmp/before.json /app/glowbank/readout.json; echo ghost_preserved=$?
rm -f /app/cardwell/ghost.card
/app/bin/lanternix readout --lamp /app/lamps/alien.lamp; echo alien_rc=$?; cat /app/glowbank/readout.json

Analysis: The rebuilt ELF now correctly decodes all four supplied cards with trimmed slot names and string values. Cast still exits 2 because Spin uses exec.Command("go", ...). Go resolves the executable using the lanternix process's inherited PATH before applying cmd.Env; /usr/local/go/bin is absent from that inherited PATH. Plan: Change Spin to use the absolute Go driver path, format and rebuild the ELF, then verify cast exits 0 and preserves native ELF output. Finally rerun the key success, uncarried-card preservation, and absent-code void tests, cleaning temporary probes afterward.
